title: A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large Language Models
grouping: Two halves split by a thin vertical grey rule, each with a large sans title (Magnitude Pruning | Wanda). Each half is a three-step row of matrices joined by small grey arrows; the score equation sits above the middle matrix and a short label under each matrix.
shapes_depth: Flat grids of square cells holding small signed integers: a 3x4 weight matrix W, a weight-importance matrix and the pruned weights. Kept entries are pale yellow, pruned or low-score entries pale blue (pruned ones rewritten as 0). The activation norm ||X||_2 is a single row of four cells shaded from pale to deep orange by value. Dashed rounded boxes mark the comparison group: one box around the whole matrix ('grouped per layer') versus one box per row ('grouped per output'), with that phrase in small italics underneath.
proposed_highlight: The proposed half is on the right and adds the orange activation-norm row as the one new ingredient; its caption bolds the letters that spell the method name ('Weights and activations'); its importance matrix is cut into per-row dashed boxes where the baseline has one box.
lesson: Use a tiny integer-valued weight matrix with cells tinted kept versus pruned, and draw the comparison group as dashed boxes (whole matrix versus one per row), so a reader can check each pruning decision by reading the numbers.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024').

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: no network drawn; worked numeric example of a pruning metric on a weight matrix

insights.structure: Two side-by-side panels split by a grey vertical rule: 'Magnitude Pruning' (Weights -> Weight Importance -> Pruned Weights) and 'Wanda' (Weights plus an activation-norm row -> Weight Importance -> Pruned Weights), each a three-step left-to-right chain of 3 x 4 matrices.
insights.data: Matrices are grids of real small integers with cells coloured yellow (kept) or light blue (pruned/zero); activation norms ||X||_2 are a row of orange-shaded cells whose depth scales with value; the scoring formula S sits above each importance matrix.
insights.emphasis: Dashed boxes show the comparison group: one box around the whole matrix ('grouped per layer') for magnitude pruning versus one dashed box per row ('grouped per output') for Wanda, and the darkest orange activation (8) visibly flips which weights survive.
insights.flow: Left to right with small grey arrows inside each panel; the two panels are read in parallel as baseline versus proposed.

arrangement.units: two unboxed panels separated by a vertical rule, each a row of three captioned matrices
arrangement.inputs_as: weight matrix with numeric entries (plus activation-norm row for Wanda)
arrangement.shared: same weight matrix values in both panels
